stage1.impression: A clean high-key image of a tinted acrylic horn on clear posts over an amber cabinet. The colour glows well against the white, but the horn's whole upper silhouette dissolves into the background, the bell's mouth is a flat yellow plane with no modelling, and the throat is a confusing tangle of red and black refractions. The frame shows the whole horn side-on with an awkward slice of cabinet at the bottom, so it reads as a cropped overview and not a deliberate macro, and it still looks like a render.

blocking_9: The horn's upper outline separates from the white: a step of at least 15 luminance across the top edge of the bell (now 1.7).
The frame is a true detail of the rolled lip and the twist-lock cap, not a side view of the whole horn with a strip of cabinet at the bottom.
The bell's interior has a readable gradient (luminance range across the mouth of at least 25, now 2.6) so it reads as a curved cast surface and not a flat yellow card.
No hard-edged CG highlight chips: the white square near the throat (about 860-900, 640-690) is gone or softened into a long graduated streak.
The throat's black and red refraction tangle is calmed so the eye goes to the lip and the cap.

defects.what: The top of the bell vanishes into the background; the outline is lost (edge step 1.7 lum, surface 251 vs background 249).
The bell's mouth is a flat, even yellow (lum 221-224 over 300x400 px); no curvature or depth reads.
Throat shows black voids and red blotches from refraction (lum p5 14, median 39); busy and dark, pulls the eye from the lip and cap.
Hard white quadrilateral highlight, the glossy flag's reflection, reads as a CG chip.
Cabinet top cut off at the frame's bottom edge, half a wordmark visible at the left (EARF letters cropped); dead weight in a detail shot.
The lip, the subject of the detail, sits against the right edge with only about 100 px of margin and is seen almost edge-on, so its roll does not read.
The twist-lock cap at the left end is seen edge-on and dark; its detail does not read.
Post head and fitting under the cap tangle with the reflections of the post behind; reads as clutter.

changes.problem: The frame is an overview of the horn plus a strip of cabinet, not a detail of the lip and the cap.

evidence.measured: The cabinet fills the bottom 25% of the frame; the lip has about 100 px of right margin; the cap is edge-on at the left.

change.to: rotate_z 150 so the mouth turns about 30 degrees toward camera and the lip's roll shows as a crescent; camera position [1.0,-2.3,1.45], target [0.0,0.02,1.18], lens 135 mm; frame the bell's lip as the large shape occupying the right two thirds, with the cap at the left third, and the cabinet's top edge either out of frame or as a thin line below 1500 px

changes.expected: The lip's rolled edge reads as a thick, light-catching crescent; the cabinet leaves the frame or becomes a thin base line; at least 120 px of white around the horn on every side.

changes.problem: The top of the bell is lit to the same white as the seamless, so the silhouette dissolves.

evidence.measured: lum_median 251 against background 249; edge step across top 1.7 lum.

change.to: add a black non-glossy flag over the horn, center [0.0, 0.0, 2.3], size [1.6, 0.6], normal [0,0,-1], plus a narrow black glossy flag 0.15 x 1.6 m at [0.6,-0.6,2.0] facing the horn so the top edge picks up a dark line; scrim irradiance 0.6

changes.expected: A clean darker amber line defines the top of the bell; outline legible all the way round.

changes.problem: The mouth's interior is a flat yellow plane with no gradient.

change.from: front-strip azimuth -25, elevation 22, ramp 0->1 over z 0.2-1.8; key azimuth -30
change.to: front-strip azimuth +35, elevation 15, distance 2.2, ramp on z 0.9->1.6 values 0->1, so a graduated streak runs down the inside of the bell; key azimuth -55 so the near half of the mouth falls off

changes.expected: The mouth shades from bright yellow at the lip to deeper amber toward the throat; a long soft streak follows the curvature.

changes.problem: A hard square white highlight in the throat reads as a CG chip.

evidence.measured: isolated near-white quad on amber ground with hard edges.

change.to: glossy false, or replace with a graduated panel 0.3 x 2.4 m with a ramp along z so its reflection is a soft streak with no ends

changes.expected: No hard-edged white shape inside the horn; any reflection there is a soft graduated streak.

changes.problem: The throat is a tangle of black voids and red blotches that pulls focus from the lip and the cap.

evidence.measured: lum_median 39, p5 14, RGB median 87,25,28: near-black red.

change.from: back-top irradiance 22 at azimuth 200 elevation 30; one reflect_only bounce in front
change.to: back-top irradiance 12, elevation 50 to reduce the hot rim; add a white reflect_only bounce card 1.5 x 1.0 m behind and below the horn at [-0.3, 0.9, 0.7] facing the horn so the throat's interior refracts white instead of black

changes.expected: The throat reads as glowing amber with soft red depth, no black voids larger than a few pixels.

changes.problem: The twist-lock cap at the left end is dark and edge-on, so the second subject of the detail does not read.

evidence.measured: dark red-brown disc, details lost in the shadow side.

change.to: on, as a white reflect_only bounce card 1.2 x 1.4 m at [-1.2,-0.4,1.2] facing the cap, so the cap's rim and its lugs catch a soft edge light

changes.expected: The cap's rim and its twist lugs show as a clean light edge against the dark disc.

changes.problem: The white is a flat, dead 249 everywhere; with the product floating there is no sense of space or light falling off.

evidence.measured: lum_range 0.2 across the whole top band.

change.to: bg-left 3.9, bg-right 3.1, for a gentle left-to-right fall of 5-8 luminance across the seamless behind the horn

changes.expected: A barely perceptible gradient behind the product; still high-key white.

out_of_scope.request: The horn reads amber to red at the throat, and only the bell reads golden yellow; check the throat's colour against the golden yellow finish.
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's colour and parts are fixed; if the red is a part's colour, not a refraction, it is a model question.

out_of_scope.request: The red blotched shapes inside the throat may be internal parts (driver, cap internals) showing through the acrylic.
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's parts are fixed; only the light can change how they read.
